preamble.summary:
Add `phax artifact revise <path> --amendment <file|-> [--by operator|machine:<grant>] [--model <id>] [--effort low|medium|high] [--json]`. It revises a Draft, headless-authored spec or plan whose sidecar is in sync. One read-only writer session returns the whole revised document carrying the amendment. It resumes the kept authoring session when that session ran on the writer's provider in this checkout, and starts a new session otherwise. phax checks the answer: its kind's current `$schema` and decode checks, every existing question unchanged and in place, and new open questions only appended. It keeps the frontmatter byte for byte, writes nothing when the body renders the same, and otherwise writes the `.md` and sidecar, re-seeds a plan's extraction cache and commits both in one commit without asking. The artifact stays Draft. The commit body carries the amendment verbatim and the trailers `Artifact`, `Revised-By` and `Revision-Id`. Where records are configured, every writer session that ran leaves one revision record keyed `revision/<Revision-Id>`, in the new persisted format `revision-record-manifest`. It is stamped with the opened version 0.38.0 through a `next` snapshot until the cut. `phax records explain <commit>` resolves a revise commit to that record.

Order: the pure checks first (phase-01), then the record format (phase-02) and its writer (phase-03). Then decide's verdicts-mode writer path is extracted into one module that decide and revise both call, with decide's behaviour unchanged (phase-04). Then come the use case's acceptance tests (phase-05) and the use case that passes them (phase-06), the CLI definition and its regenerated contract files (phase-07), `records explain` (phase-08), and the docs, which also correct decide's stale Vibe sentences (phase-09).

The spec's sidecar does not exist, so test lines carry no criterion id; each test names the §8 criterion it covers in its title. Q1 is decided: a writer routed to Mistral Vibe runs read-only on the shared writer path, exactly as decide's does, and revise has no Vibe guard.
preamble.requiredCommandsNote: `pnpm exec tsx` runs `scripts/schemas-check.ts --write` in phase-02, which writes the revision record's `next` snapshot and regenerates `src/schemas/release.ts`, `packages/schemas/src/generated/index.ts` and `packages/schemas/shipped-json.json`. `pnpm gen:usage-spec` and `pnpm docs:cli` regenerate `phax.usage.kdl` and `docs/cli/reference.md` from the command definitions in phase-07, phase-08 and phase-09. All three are already entries of `security.agentCommands` in phax.json, so phax.json needs no change.
technicalArbitrations: How revise and decide share the writer path. Decide's verdicts-mode writer moves into one module, `src/app/headlessWriter.ts`, that both use cases call (phase-04). It holds the choice of session (the kept authoring session only when it decodes, ran on the routed provider and ran in this checkout), the writer turn with its one corrective resume, and the landing step: before/after/diff files, the concurrent-edit check, the plan-cache seed, the write and the one commit. Each is parameterized by what the answer is checked against (a check function), the retry prompt, the commit message and error factories supplied by the caller. Decide's code must not change in behaviour: its refusal messages and `DecideRefusedError` reasons, `DecideDocumentError`, its exit codes, the `decide/<id>/<NN>/` folder and its file names, its prompts, its commit message, its decision record and its report. The proof is that decide's suites pass without an edit (`tests/integration/decideVerdicts.test.ts`, `decideVerdictsPlanHand.test.ts`, `decideArtifact.test.ts`, `artifactDecideVerdictsCommand.test.ts`, `writeDecisionRecord.test.ts`, `tests/unit/cli/artifactDecideVerdicts.test.ts`, `tests/helpers/decideVerdictsHarness.ts`). Loss knowingly accepted: a refactor of decide's working path inside a feature plan, contained by those untouched suites. Extending `decideVerdicts.ts` with a revise mode was rejected because it would mix revise's refusals, record and commit into decide's module and error classes.

What counts as a change to an existing question (§5.5, §5.6, Q1 frozen-append). Questions are compared by structural JSON equality: key order is not content, array order is (decide's `sameJson`). Every key counts: id, question, options and their order, recommendation, rationale, and on an arbitrated question its verdict (`by` and `at` included) and history. The revised `arbitratedQuestions` must equal the original exactly. The revised `openQuestions` must begin with the original open questions, element for element. Anything after them is a new open question, and its id must be new to the artifact. So an edited, removed, reordered, reopened or newly arbitrated question is refused, and so is a question appended to the arbitrated array. Loss knowingly accepted: a writer that inserts a new open question between existing ones is refused (and corrected once), though no existing question changed.

The revision record's shape, beside the decision record's. `kind: "revision"`, `revisionId` (`<authoringId>/<NN>`), `artifact`, `artifactKind`, `session` (`new` | `resumed-authoring`), `requester` (`{ kind: "operator", name }` | `{ kind: "machine", grant }`), `newQuestions` (the appended ids), `sourceSha` (HEAD as the session starts), `shape`, `provider`, `model` (concrete), `requestedModel`, `effort`, `usage`, then the outcome: `committed` with `commit`, `unchanged` with `commit: null`, or `failed` with `commit: null` and `failure`. It drops the decision record's `mode`, `doctrine`, `questions`, `arbitrated` and `departed`, since a revision has no doctrine and no verdict. `failure` is the revision record's own literal schema, with the same members as `DecisionFailure`; a type test keeps the two equal. The record carries `amendment.md`, `prompt.md`, `retry-prompt.md`, `document.json`, `body.diff` and the two transcripts per `records.transcript`, and never a provider session id. Losses knowingly accepted: a third outcome (`unchanged`) beyond the spec's `committed or failed`, so that every writer session that ran is recorded (§5.16); and a failure enum duplicated, not shared, so the new format does not move when the decision record's does.

The writer's prompt shows the amendment as a change request against the current document, not as a brief addendum (spec §10 left this open). The prompt gives the current document and the amendment. It asks for the whole document with the amendment carried wherever it applies and everything else left as it is. A new session also gets the kind's authoring skill and the kept brief as background. Loss knowingly accepted: an amendment that would justify rethinking the artifact's decomposition gets a minimal edit; re-authoring stays the path for that.
The `--amendment` spelling (indicative in the spec) is kept as `--amendment <file|->`, read by the command library as a text stdin document like `--brief`.

`records explain` resolves a revise commit from its last paragraph only. When the commit message's last paragraph (its trailer block) holds `Revision-Id`, the address is the revision record, checked before every other trailer. Otherwise today's whole-body trailer reading applies unchanged. A verbatim amendment line shaped like a trailer (`Authoring-Id: …`, `Run-Id: …`) therefore never addresses another record. Loss knowingly accepted: two trailer readings in one function.

Model and effort follow headless authoring (§6): `--model`/`--effort`, else phax.json's resolved `authoring.<kind>` (which carries the catalog default when phax.json sets none), routed through `resolveModel` like authoring. The report names the source as `flag` or `authoring.<kind>`. Effort is one of `low | medium | high`.

The requester resolves through `src/app/resolveArbiter.ts`, as `phax artifact reopen` does: `--by operator`, `--by machine:<grant>`, or with no `--by` the operator when stdin is a terminal. A committing git identity (`git.committerName`) is required in every case, because the revision commits (§5.18).

No change (§5.9) is judged on the rendered body. The revised document's rendering (`renderCurrent`) is compared with the current body (`artifactBody`) through `sameRendering`, the comparison sidecar agreement uses. A document whose rendered body is the same writes nothing, even when a field that does not render differs.

A writer routed to Mistral Vibe runs read-only, as decide's verdicts writer does (Q1, run-read-only). The spec was corrected on 2026-11-13: §5.15 and its criterion now read 'A writer routed to Vibe runs read-only'. Revise has no Vibe guard and no `provider-read-only` refusal. Loss knowingly accepted: a Vibe writer is confined by Vibe's tool-level read-only posture (`read_file` and `grep`) rather than Claude Code's or Codex's, so a session misconfigured around its accept-edits agent is the only thing between it and a write. Decide's help and `docs/arbitration.md` still say a Vibe-routed writer is refused; phase-09 corrects them.

phases.title: Revise's pure checks, commit message and prompt
phases.objective: Give revise its pure core: the question-freeze check, the decode of a revised answer with the plan's lineage restored, the no-change judgement, the commit message with its trailers, and the writer's prompt and retry prompt. Later phases call these without re-deciding them.
detailedInstructions: Read `src/domain/decide/revision.ts` first. Reuse its exported helpers (`RevisionRefusal`, `describeRevisionRefusal`, `refusal`, `arraysOf`, `sameJson`, `firstDifference`, `answerStampViolation`, `firstParseIssue`, `locate`, `isObject`, `renderRevisedArtifact`) by import. Do not change that module's behaviour; export one more helper from it only if needed (it is in the optional list).
Create `src/domain/revise/revision.ts` (pure, no I/O) exporting:

`firstQuestionFreezeViolation(before: SidecarDocument, after: SidecarDocument): RevisionRefusal | undefined`. Checks, in order and with document-relative paths (`openQuestions[1]` on a spec, `preamble.openQuestions[1]` on a plan, via `arraysOf(...).basePath`): (1) the kinds are the same; (2) `after.arbitratedQuestions` equals `before.arbitratedQuestions` exactly by `sameJson`; (3) `after.openQuestions` begins with every element of `before.openQuestions` at the same index, each `sameJson`-equal; (4) each open question after that prefix has an id that is not the id of any question of `before`. A difference in an existing question names it in the spec's words, e.g. `the writer changed question Q2 — a revision never touches a question; decide it with phax artifact decide`. A missing question says it was removed, an existing id at another index says it was moved, a question added to `arbitratedQuestions` says new questions are appended to the open questions only, and a reused id says it is already a question of the artifact.
`appendedOpenQuestions(before, after): ReadonlyArray<{ readonly id: string; readonly question: string }>`: the open questions after the original prefix, in order.

`restoreLineage(json: unknown, original: SidecarDocument): unknown`: for a plan, sets `sourceSpec` and `completesSpec` from the original on an object answer (as `stampSessionVerdicts` does for decide); a spec answer, or a non-object, is returned as is; never mutates its input.

`decodeRevisedAnswer(json: unknown, original: SidecarDocument): Result<{ document: SidecarDocument; newQuestions: ReadonlyArray<{ id; question }> }, RevisionRefusal>`. It refuses with `answerStampViolation(kind, json)` at `$schema` (or `""` for a non-object). Then it decodes `restoreLineage(json, original)` with `decodeCurrentDocumentSidecar(kind, …)` from `src/schemas/persisted.ts`, mapped through `firstParseIssue`; that decode runs a spec's traceability checks and a plan's decode checks. Then it applies `firstQuestionFreezeViolation`. On success it returns the decoded document and `appendedOpenQuestions`.
`rendersSameBody(currentMd: string, after: SidecarDocument): boolean`: `sameRendering(artifactBody(currentMd), renderCurrent(after))` from `src/domain/artifact/sidecar.ts`.

A requester type `RevisionRequester = { kind: "operator"; name: string } | { kind: "machine"; grant: string }`. Read `ResolvedArbiter` in `src/domain/artifact/arbiter.ts` first: if it already has this shape, re-export it under this name; otherwise define it here.
`revisedByTrailer(requester): string` returns `operator (<name>)` or `machine (<grant>)`.

`reviseCommitMessage({ kind, slug, path, amendment, model, effort, provider, requester, revisionId }): { subject; body }`. The subject is `docs(specs): revise <slug>` or `docs(plans): revise <slug>`. The body is exactly, line by line: `Revised headless (<model> / <effort>, <provider>) from this amendment:`, an empty line, the amendment text with trailing whitespace and newlines removed at its end only (otherwise verbatim), an empty line, then `Artifact: <path>`, `Revised-By: <revisedByTrailer>`, `Revision-Id: <revisionId>`. It must match the spec §6 example byte for byte.

Create `src/domain/revise/prompt.ts` (pure) exporting `buildRevisePrompt(input)` and `buildReviseRetryPrompt(refusal: string): string`. The input is `{ kind, artifactPath, session: "new" | "resume", skillText, brief: string | null, document: SidecarDocument, amendment: string, schemaUrl: string }`.

The prompt states what a revision is and its rules. Return the whole document as one JSON object with `$schema` equal to `schemaUrl`, as the final message alone. Carry the amendment into the body wherever it applies and leave everything else as it is. Never change, remove or reorder a question, open or arbitrated. A new ambiguity the amendment raises may be appended at the end of the open questions under a new id. `sourceSpec`, `completesSpec` and the frontmatter are not revised. Write no files.

Then the prompt gives the current document as JSON (from `serializeSidecar(document)`) and the amendment under its own heading, verbatim. A `new` session's prompt also opens with the authoring skill text verbatim and, when `brief` is not null, the brief under a heading saying it is the brief the artifact was authored from. A `resume` prompt omits the skill and the brief, which the session already holds.
`buildReviseRetryPrompt` names the refusal and asks for the whole document again under the same rules.

Write the tests listed in the test strategy, with made-up spec and plan documents. Build them from the existing fixtures in `tests/unit/decide/verdictsFixtures.ts` where they fit; otherwise build them in the test files.

phases.title: The revision record manifest format
phases.objective: Register `revision-record-manifest` as a persisted format phax can write and every reader can read. It is born with `$schema` and stamped 0.38.0 through a `next` snapshot, has its JSON Schema, and is published by the schemas package. Records listing and records explain recognise it as a record kind.
detailedInstructions: Follow how `review-record-manifest` was added (grep the repository for it outside docs/): every place it is registered, a revision record is registered the same way.

Create `src/schemas/revisionRecord.ts`, modelled on `src/schemas/decisionRecord.ts`, with the shape from the Technical arbitrations. Common fields: `kind: Literal("revision")`; `revisionId` (pattern `^[^/\s]+\/\d{2,}$`, described as `<authoringId>/<NN>, the Revision-Id trailer`); `artifact` (NonEmptyString); `artifactKind` (`spec` | `plan`); `session` (`new` | `resumed-authoring`); `requester`, a union of `{ kind: "operator", name: NonEmptyString }` and `{ kind: "machine", grant: NonEmptyString }`; `newQuestions` (array of NonEmptyString); `sourceSha`; `shape` (`RecordShapeSchema`); `provider` (`ProviderIdSchema`); `model`; `requestedModel`; `effort`; `usage` (`TokenUsageSchema`).

It has three variants: `outcome: "committed"` with `commit: NonEmptyString`; `outcome: "unchanged"` with `commit: Null`; and `outcome: "failed"` with `commit: Null` and `failure: RevisionFailureSchema`. `RevisionFailureSchema` has the same literals as `DecisionFailureSchema`. Add a type-level equality between the two in the type tests.

Export `RevisionRecordManifestFileSchema` (each variant with `$schema: schemaUrlField("revision-record-manifest")`), `RevisionRecordManifestFile`, `RevisionRecordManifest` (without `$schema`), `RevisionRecordOutcome`, `RevisionFailure`, `decodeRevisionRecordManifestFile` (onExcessProperty error), `encodeRevisionRecordManifest` and `isRevisionRecordManifest` (kind === "revision"). There is no lift function and no history module: the format is born at this release.

Register the format: append `revision-record-manifest` to `FORMAT_IDS` and to `SCHEMA_BORN_FORMAT_IDS` in `src/schemas/schemaUrl.ts` (at the end, keeping existing order), and extend the doc comments there. In `src/schemas/persisted.ts`, add its reader and every per-format entry the compiler asks for. In `readRecordManifestFile`, dispatch `kind: "revision"` to it, and add it to the `RecordManifest` union.

In the schemas package: add `revisionRecordManifestFormat`, `parseRevisionRecordManifest`, `toLatestRevisionRecordManifest`, `LatestRevisionRecordManifest`, `RevisionRecordManifestShapes` and `RevisionRecordManifestShape` in `packages/schemas/src/formats/recordManifests.ts`. Add it to `RecordManifestShapes`, `recordManifestFormats` and `parseRecordManifest`: `kind: "revision"` is read as a revision record manifest, born with `$schema`, and its doc comment says so. Export everything from `packages/schemas/src/index.ts` (`RevisionRecordManifestSchema`, `RevisionRecordManifest`, …) as for the review record. Add the format to `packages/schemas/build/jsonSchemas.ts`: `FORMAT_DEFINITIONS`, the excess map (`error`) and `RECORD_MANIFEST_MEMBERS`.

Run `pnpm exec tsx scripts/schemas-check.ts --write`. It creates `packages/schemas/snapshots/revision-record-manifest/next.schema.json`, sets `CURRENT_STAMPS["revision-record-manifest"]` to `0.38.0` in `src/schemas/release.ts`, and updates `packages/schemas/src/generated/index.ts` and `packages/schemas/shipped-json.json`. Never edit those generated files by hand. Then run `pnpm exec tsx scripts/schemas-check.ts` (no flag) and make it pass.

Add the behaviour corpus cases `tests/behaviourCorpus/cases/formats/revision-record-manifest.json` and `tests/behaviourCorpus/cases/encode/revision-record-manifest.json`, modelled on the review record's: one valid document per outcome, and refusals for an unknown key, a committed record with `commit: null`, a failed record without `failure`, and a missing `$schema`. Register the subject in `tests/behaviourCorpus/subjects.ts` and the coverage list in `tests/unit/behaviourCorpus/coverage.test.ts`. Update `tests/behaviourCorpus/baseline/snapshot-digests.json` only if its check asks for it.

Update every per-format test table that the compiler or a test failure names: `tests/unit/schemaUrl.test.ts`, `tests/unit/architecturalGuards.test.ts` (the schema module list and the decoder map), `tests/type/schemasPackage.ts` (exports, Equals checks, unions), and the `tests/unit/schemasPackage/` files `documents.ts` (a valid revision manifest), `documents.test.ts`, `parity.test.ts`, `currentShapes.test.ts`, `jsonSchemas.test.ts`, `recordManifests.test.ts` (parse, toLatest and refusals as for the review record, with the stamp `0.38.0`) and `exports.test.ts`.

The `RecordManifest` union now includes a revision manifest, so its consumers must handle it. In `src/app/recordsList.ts`, add a list entry `{ kind: "revision", revisionId, shape, outcome, recordCommitSha, artifact, artifactKind }` before the phase fallback. In `src/cli/definitions/records.ts`, add its output schema member and its row (`revision`, id, shape, outcome, artifact). In `src/app/recordsExplain.ts`, change only `manifestKindLabel`, which gains `a revision manifest`. Explain's resolution of `Revision-Id` is phase-08's.

Add a row to the README `## Persisted formats` table, after the decision record's: `Revision record manifest` | `revision-record-manifest` | `revision/<authoringId>/<NN>/record.json` on `phax/records/v1` | `parseRevisionRecordManifest` | `json/revision-record-manifest.schema.json`.

Create `tests/unit/revisionRecord.test.ts`: decode and encode round trip for each outcome; refusals for an unknown key and for each mismatched outcome/commit pair; the type equality between `RevisionFailure` and `DecisionFailure` if it is not already in `tests/type/`.
If `records list --json`'s output schema appears in `phax.usage.kdl` or `docs/cli/reference.md` and the usage drift tests fail, run `pnpm gen:usage-spec` and `pnpm docs:cli`.

phases.title: The revision record writer
phases.objective: Write one revision record per writer session on `phax/records/v1`, keyed `revision/<Revision-Id>`, with the revision folder's files and a manifest stamped with the new format. The revise use case can then record every end, committed, unchanged or failed.
detailedInstructions: Create `src/app/writeRevisionRecord.ts`, modelled on `src/app/writeDecisionRecord.ts` (verdicts mode), reusing `resolveRecordDestination`, `commitRecordTree`, `computeSessionUsage` and `RECORD_TRANSCRIPT_FILE` from `src/app/recordPlumbing.ts` and `selectRecordArtifacts` from `src/domain/records/assemble.ts`.

Export the revision folder's file names: `REVISE_AMENDMENT_FILENAME = "amendment.md"`, `REVISE_PROMPT_FILENAME = "prompt.md"`, `REVISE_RETRY_PROMPT_FILENAME = "retry-prompt.md"`, `REVISE_TRANSCRIPT_FILENAME = RECORD_TRANSCRIPT_FILE`, `REVISE_RETRY_TRANSCRIPT_FILENAME = "retry-output.jsonl"`, `REVISE_DOCUMENT_FILENAME = "document.json"`, `REVISE_BEFORE_FILENAME = "before.md"`, `REVISE_AFTER_FILENAME = "after.md"` and `REVISE_DIFF_FILENAME = "body.diff"`. The recorded files are amendment, prompt, retry prompt, document, diff and the two transcripts; the transcripts are kept or dropped together under `records.transcript`, and before/after are never recorded.

Export `revisionRecordKey(revisionId) = revision/<revisionId>` and `RevisionRecordEnd` = `{ outcome: "committed"; commit: string }` | `{ outcome: "unchanged"; commit: null }` | `{ outcome: "failed"; commit: null; failure: RevisionFailure }`.

Export `writeRevisionRecord(input)`. Its input has `repoRoot`, `recordsClonePath?`, `records`, `publishRemote`, `folder`, `revisionId`, `artifact`, `artifactKind`, `session`, `requester`, `newQuestions`, `sourceSha`, `provider`, `model`, `requestedModel`, `effort`, `end`, `retried`, `turnSessionIds` and `sessionIds`. Usage counts the first turn and, when retried, the retry, each with its session id.

The manifest is encoded through `encodeRevisionRecordManifest(withSchemaUrl("revision-record-manifest", manifest))`. The records commit message is `records(revision): <outcome>`, an empty line, then `Revision-Id: <revisionId>`, `Artifact: <artifact>`, `Shape: <shape>`. Every session id in `sessionIds` is redacted from the recorded files. With records off it does nothing, exactly as the decision writer.

Export `RevisionRecordStatus` (the write result, or `{ kind: "write-failed"; message }`), `RevisionRecordPush` (a push result or `{ kind: "no-record" }`), `revisionRecordWarning(record, followingFailedSession?)` and `revisionRecordPushWarning(push)`, worded as the decision ones with `revision record` in place of `decision record`.

Create `tests/integration/writeRevisionRecord.test.ts`, modelled on `tests/integration/writeDecisionRecord.test.ts`, in a temp repository with an in-repo destination. It covers: a committed record's key, its manifest decoded by `decodeRevisionRecordManifestFile` with `$schema` at 0.38.0, its files and the records commit message; an unchanged and a failed record; transcripts dropped under `records.transcript: false`; a session id redacted from a recorded prompt; records off writing nothing.

Extend `tests/integration/persistedProducer.test.ts` so that `writeRevisionRecord`'s `record.json` is checked like every other producer's: it decodes under its format's current schema and its stamp is the current one.

phases.title: One headless writer path for decide and revise
phases.objective: Extract decide's verdicts-mode writer path into `src/app/headlessWriter.ts`, parameterized so that revise can call it. Decide keeps every behaviour it has today, as its untouched test suites show.
detailedInstructions: Create `src/app/headlessWriter.ts` by moving code out of `src/app/decideVerdicts.ts` and `src/app/decideArtifact.ts`. Decide then calls the moved code. Do not rewrite the logic.

Move `chooseWriterSession` and its `WriterSession` type, taking `{ stateRoot, repoRoot, artifactId, provider }`. The rule stays the same: resume the kept authoring session only when `session.json` decodes, names the routed provider and ran in this checkout (`resolve(cwd) === resolve(repoRoot)`); prefer `retrySessionId`; otherwise start a new session.

Move `runWriter` as a function generic over the accepted answer `A` and the refusal error `E`. Its parameters are: `check(result: AgentRunResult): Result<A, RevisionRefusal>`; `retryPrompt(refusal: string): string`; `refusedWarning(refusal: string): string` (the warn line); `rejectedTwice(path: string, message: string): E`; the transcript and retry-prompt file names; the agent options (always `readOnly: true`); and an observed object `{ retried, sessionIds, accepted }`. Provider errors and limits are never retried. A second refusal fails with `rejectedTwice`, its message naming both refusals as today.

Move the landing step as two functions, so that revise can stop between them on no change. `diffAnswer({ folder, repoRoot, path, beforeMd, afterMd, documentJson, fileNames })` writes document.json, before.md, after.md and body.diff and returns the diff. `landAnswer({ repoRoot, stateRoot, path, snapshotMd, snapshotSidecarText, md, sidecarText, planDocument, extractPlanModel, extractPlanEffort, nowIso, commitMessage, changed: (path: string, which) => E })` does the concurrent-edit check (refusing through `changed`, leaving the change in place), seeds a plan's extraction cache before writing, writes the `.md` and the sidecar, commits exactly those paths, and fails with `ArtifactCommitFailedError` when the commit fails. It returns `{ paths, commit: { hash, subject } }`.

Extract the shared artifact reading out of `readArtifact` in `src/app/decideArtifact.ts` into `readDraftArtifact`. It takes `{ path, repoRoot }` and the caller's words: a `refuse(reason, message) => E` factory, the verb used in `only a Draft artifact is <verb>`, and what a hand-authored artifact gets (`parse` its §9 as decide does, or a refusal the caller builds). Its order is: validate, Draft only (an Approved or Stale artifact names `phax artifact reopen <path>`), uncommitted changes on the write set, then the sidecar in sync and current, or the hand-authored branch. `readArtifact` delegates to it with decide's `refused`, `decided` and `parse`. Every decide message stays byte for byte as it is.

`decideVerdicts.ts` now calls `chooseWriterSession`, `runWriter`, `diffAnswer` and `landAnswer` with its own check (`checkAnswer`), `buildDecideRetryPrompt`, its warn wording, `DecideDocumentError`, `DECIDE_*` file names, `verdictsCommitMessage` and `refused("changed", …)`. Its exported names, input, result, record and report stay the same. Keep `nextDecisionIndex` exported from `decideArtifact.ts`; revise imports it.

Do not edit any of decide's tests or its harness: `tests/integration/decideVerdicts.test.ts`, `tests/integration/decideVerdictsPlanHand.test.ts`, `tests/integration/decideArtifact.test.ts`, `tests/integration/artifactDecideVerdictsCommand.test.ts`, `tests/integration/writeDecisionRecord.test.ts`, `tests/unit/cli/artifactDecideVerdicts.test.ts`, `tests/helpers/decideVerdictsHarness.ts`. They must pass as they are. If one fails, the refactor changed a behaviour: fix the refactor, not the test.

Create `tests/integration/headlessWriter.test.ts` for what decide's suites do not pin through the parameters. With the fake backend from `src/infra/fakes/backend.js` and a temp git repository: a session-choice table (no session.json, undecodable, another provider, another cwd, a match with and without a retry id); `runWriter` calls the caller's `rejectedTwice` on a second refusal and never resumes after a usage limit; `landAnswer` refuses through the caller's `changed` when the artifact changed, leaving the change in the working tree and HEAD as it was.

The contract: the caller supplies what the answer is checked against, how a refusal is worded, the error each failure becomes, the folder's file names and the commit message. The module guarantees a read-only writer, at most one corrective resume, nothing written to the repository before the answer passed and the artifact is unchanged on disk, and one commit holding exactly the artifact and its sidecar.

phases.objective: Freeze the spec's acceptance criteria as executable tests at the revise use case's entry, against a stub that fails recognisably. phase-06 then implements the use case against tests it cannot bend.
detailedInstructions: Create the stub `src/app/reviseArtifact.ts`. It declares the full input and result types and a `reviseArtifact(input)` function whose body is `Effect.die(new Error("not implemented: reviseArtifact (phase-06)"))`. Its requirement is `FileSystem | Git | GitHub | Backend | Terminal`.

The stub's `ReviseArtifactInput` holds: `path` (repo-relative); `amendment: { text: string; label: string }` (label is the path as given, or `stdin`); `by: string | undefined`; `model` and `effort: string | undefined`; `authoring: Readonly<Record<ArtifactKind, { model: string; effort: Effort }>>` (phax.json's resolved `authoring.spec` and `authoring.plan`); `routing: ModelRouting`; `providerConfig: ProviderConfig`; `skills: Readonly<Record<ArtifactKind, string>>` (the `phax-spec` and `phax-planning` SKILL.md texts); `security: ResolvedSecurityConfig`; `repoRoot`; `stateRoot`; `extractPlanModel`; `extractPlanEffort`; `nowIso`; `records: ResolvedRecordsConfig`; `recordsClonePath?`; `publishRemote`; and `output: Pick<OutputPort, "log" | "warn">`.

The stub's `ReviseArtifactResult` holds: `kind` (`committed` | `unchanged`); `path`; `paths` (empty when unchanged); `status: "Draft"`; `session` (`new` | `resumed-authoring`); `provider`; `model` (concrete); `requestedModel`; `effort`; `modelSource` (`flag` | `authoring.spec` | `authoring.plan`); `effortSource` (same three); `requester` (`RevisionRequester` from phase-01); `newQuestions: ReadonlyArray<{ id: string; question: string }>`; `diff`; `commit: { hash; subject } | null`; `revisionId`; `record: RevisionRecordStatus`; and `recordPush: RevisionRecordPush` (from phase-03). Declare `ReviseArtifactError` as a union of the existing error classes decide's verdicts mode uses; phase-06 may widen it.

Create `tests/helpers/reviseHarness.ts`, modelled on `tests/helpers/decideVerdictsHarness.ts` and reusing its building blocks by import where they fit (`isolateGit`, `isolatePhaxHome`, `tempGit`, the fake backend, the fake terminal and the fake GitHub). It provides a temp git repository with a committer identity and a state root beside it. Its seeders write a Draft headless spec and a Draft headless plan with in-sync sidecars, plus their kept `session.json` (provider and cwd chosen per test) and `brief.md` under `authoring/<authoringId>/`. It also seeds a hand-authored plan, a diverged sidecar, an invalid sidecar and a sidecar stamped below its shape (an older `$schema`), and can set the status to Approved or Stale. It configures in-repo records. It runs `reviseArtifact` and returns the Result, and it maps a failure to its exit code with `exitCodeForAuthoringError` from `src/cli/commands/runLayers.ts`, as the decide harness does. Its helpers read HEAD, the porcelain status, a repo file, the plan extraction cache, the records branch and the state root's `revise/` folder.

Create `tests/unit/revise/reviseFixtures.ts` with made-up documents and writer answers: a spec and a plan, each with one open and one arbitrated question; a valid revised plan answer and a valid revised spec answer (one body field changed, `$schema` current); an answer appending one open question `Q9`; answers that edit an arbitrated verdict's `why`, remove the open question, and reorder two questions (give the plan fixture a second open question for this); prose; a document without `$schema`; a plan answer with a different `sourceSpec`; and the current document unchanged. Every name and operator is made up.

Create `tests/integration/reviseArtifact.test.ts`. Name each test after the §8 criterion it covers. Mark every test with vitest's expected-failure marker (`it.fails(...)`), so the gate stays green against the stub. The tests:

(1) A plan is revised from an amendment. The kept session is on the writer's provider in this checkout and `--by operator` is given. Expect one new commit holding exactly the `.md` and the sidecar. The extraction cache holds the new document (seeded for the new `.md`). `inspectSidecar` agrees `in-sync` and the frontmatter status is Draft. `result.session` is `resumed-authoring`, and the backend saw a resume, not a run.

(2) A spec is revised in a new session. The kept session ran on another provider. The backend saw a new run whose prompt contains the current document's text, the kept brief and the amendment, and `result.session` is `new`.
(3) Only a Draft is revised. An Approved plan, then a Stale one: each exits 12 with a message naming `phax artifact reopen <path>`, the backend saw no call, and HEAD is unchanged.

(4) Only a headless artifact in sync is revised. A hand-authored plan (message names editing the .md directly), a diverged sidecar, an invalid sidecar and one stamped below its shape (message names `phax artifact migrate-documents`): each exits 12 before any call.

(5) A changed question is refused. A writer that edits an arbitrated verdict, removes an open question, or reorders two questions: each time the first answer is refused, exactly one corrective resume runs, the second refused answer exits 5, and the artifact, sidecar and HEAD are unchanged.

(6) A new open question is accepted. The commit lands with `Q9` in the sidecar's open questions and in the `.md` under `## Open questions` (plan) or `## 9. Open questions` (spec), and `result.newQuestions` lists `Q9`.

(7) A malformed answer is refused. Prose then, on the corrective resume, a document without `$schema`: exit 5, with the failure's message naming the `$schema` violation, and the working tree clean with HEAD unchanged.
(8) Frontmatter is kept. The answer has a different `sourceSpec`; after the commit, the frontmatter block's bytes equal those before.
(9) No change is not a commit. The answer is the current document: `result.kind` is `unchanged`, `result.commit` is null, and HEAD and the porcelain status are unchanged.

(10) The commit carries the amendment and the requester. With `by: "machine:plan-loop"`: the subject is `docs(plans): revise <slug>`, the body contains the amendment verbatim, and the trailers are `Artifact: <path>`, `Revised-By: machine (plan-loop)` and `Revision-Id: <authoringId>/01`.
(11) No requester without a terminal. No `by` and a fake terminal reporting no TTY: exit 12, with a message naming `--by operator` and `--by machine:<grant>`, and no backend call.
(12) A concurrent edit is kept. Use the fake backend's `setOnResumeAgent` to edit the plan file: exit 12, the edit still in the working tree, HEAD unchanged, and no file of revise's written.

(13) A writer routed to Vibe runs read-only. A provider config enabling `mistral-vibe` and a model routed to it, as in decideVerdicts.test.ts's Vibe case: the backend's run call has `provider: "mistral-vibe"` and `readOnly: true`, `result.provider` is `mistral-vibe`, and the revision commits (one commit holding the `.md` and the sidecar).

(14) The revision is explained, record half. With records configured, a committed revision leaves a record under `revision/<revisionId>/record.json` on the records branch, stamped `revision-record-manifest`. A revision that fails with exit 5 leaves a record with outcome `failed` and failure `answer-refused`.
(15) A provider failure writes nothing. A usage limit exits 8, then a session failure of kind `network` exits 14. Each time the artifact, its sidecar and HEAD are unchanged.

(16) Uncommitted changes are refused. An uncommitted edit to the sidecar exits 12, and so does a repository with no `user.name` (unset it in the temp repo's config). Neither makes a backend call, and HEAD is unchanged.

(17) The revision's files are kept. After a commit, `<stateRoot>/revise/<authoringId>/01/` holds `amendment.md` (the amendment's text), `prompt.md`, `output.jsonl`, `document.json` and `body.diff`, and `<authoringId>/01` equals the commit's `Revision-Id` trailer.

Each test asserts the behaviour the spec states through the use case's entry, its Result, the repository and the state root. Never assert internal helpers or call order. Against the stub, every test must fail because `reviseArtifact` dies with the not-implemented error, never because of a missing module, export or type. Run the suite and confirm that every test reports as an expected failure.
The JSON report (§5.13 `--json`) and the bad-amendment refusal (§5.19) are the command's surface, tested in-phase by phase-07. The `records explain` half of criterion 14 is phase-08's.

phases.title: The revise use case on the shared writer path
phases.objective: Implement `reviseArtifact` on the shared headless writer path: every refusal before any session, one read-only writer session with one corrective resume, the no-change ending, the write and commit, and a revision record for every session that ran. It passes the acceptance tests of phase-05.
detailedInstructions: Implement `src/app/reviseArtifact.ts` behind the stub's types without changing any field of its input or result. Its errors may widen.

Add two errors to `src/domain/errors.ts`. `ReviseRefusedError` carries `reason` (`not-draft` | `sidecar` | `hand-authored` | `dirty` | `no-by` | `by` | `identity` | `model` | `changed`) and a `message` that starts `Revise refused: `. `ReviseDocumentError` carries `path` and `message`. In `src/cli/commands/runLayers.ts`, map `ReviseRefusedError` to 12 and `ReviseDocumentError` to 5 in `exitCodeForError`, and wherever `exitCodeForAuthoringError` defers to it.

Preconditions, in this order, none writing anything: (1) `refuseUnmigratedDocuments("Revise refused")` (exit 12 naming `phax artifact migrate-documents`). (2) `readDraftArtifact` from `src/app/headlessWriter.ts` with revise's words: the verb `revised`; an Approved or Stale artifact names `phax artifact reopen <path>`; uncommitted changes on the artifact or its sidecar are refused; a hand-authored artifact is refused as `<path> is hand-authored (no sidecar) — edit the .md directly`; a diverged or invalid sidecar names `sidecarRemedy`'s two remedies; an unmigrated sidecar names migrate-documents. (3) The requester through `resolveArbiter(input.by, repoRoot)` from `src/app/resolveArbiter.ts`; with no `--by` and no terminal, refuse (`no-by`) naming `--by operator` and `--by machine:<grant>`. If its own refusal already names both, keep its words; otherwise re-word it. (4) A committing identity: `git.committerName(repoRoot)` must name one, else refuse (`identity`) naming `git config user.name`. (5) The model: `resolveAuthoringSelection` with the flags and `input.authoring[kind]`; an effort outside `low | medium | high` is refused (`model`); then `resolveModel` routes it as headless authoring does. Sources are `flag` or `authoring.<kind>`. There is no provider guard: per Q1 (run-read-only) a writer routed to `mistral-vibe` runs read-only on the shared writer path, exactly as decide's verdicts writer does, and revise adds no refusal for any provider.

Then the session: `chooseWriterSession` from the shared module. The index is `nextDecisionIndex(<stateRoot>/revise/<authoringId>)`. The revision id is `<authoringId>/<NN>` and the folder is `<stateRoot>/revise/<authoringId>/<NN>/`. Write `amendment.md` (the text as given) and `prompt.md` there before the session.

Build the prompt with `buildRevisePrompt`: kind, path, session kind, `input.skills[kind]`, the kept brief from `authoringSessionFolder(stateRoot, authoringId)/brief.md` when it exists (else null), the current document, the amendment, and `currentSchemaUrl("<kind>-document")`.

Progress lines through `output.log`: `revise <kind> <slug> — amendment from <label> — headless, resumed authoring session|new session`, then the model line as decide words it (concrete model / effort (source) on provider, plus `requested <model>` when routing chose another). The record's `sourceSha` is HEAD.

Run the writer through `runWriter` with read-only agent options, `answerSchema: { call: "revise" (or the closest existing structured-call id; read `src/domain/session/structuredCalls.ts` and add a `revise` entry there if calls are enumerated), schema: answerJsonSchema("<kind>-document") }`, and `cwd: repoRoot`.

The check: `answerJson(result)`, then `decodeRevisedAnswer(json, snapshot document)`. On success, render with `renderRevisedArtifact(snapshot.md, document)` to get `{ md, sidecarText }` and keep the new questions. The retry prompt is `buildReviseRetryPrompt`, and `rejectedTwice` builds a `ReviseDocumentError` whose message names both refusals.

On an accepted answer, write `document.json`. If `rendersSameBody(snapshot.md, document)`, write `body.diff` empty, write nothing to the repository, and end `unchanged` (commit null, paths empty). Otherwise `diffAnswer`, then `landAnswer` with `reviseCommitMessage(...)` and `changed` building `ReviseRefusedError("changed", "<path> changed while the revise session ran — its change is left in place; rerun revise")`.

Every end after the writer started is recorded with `writeRevisionRecord`, then pushed with `pushRecordsBranch`, as decideVerdicts does. The end is committed (with the commit hash), unchanged, or failed with `revisionFailureOf(error)`. A record failure degrades to `write-failed` and never fails the revision. A failure is re-raised with the record's warnings as follow-ups (`failWithFollowUps`).

Create `src/app/reviseFailure.ts` exporting `revisionFailureOf(error): RevisionFailure`, as `decisionFailureOf`: a session failure gives its kind, a rate or usage limit gives its limit kind, `ReviseDocumentError` gives `answer-refused`, `ArtifactCommitFailedError` gives `commit-failed`, `ReviseRefusedError` with reason `changed` gives `artifact-changed`, and anything else gives `unknown`. Create `tests/unit/reviseFailure.test.ts` covering the full table.

Remove the `.fails` marker from every test in `tests/integration/reviseArtifact.test.ts`. Remove only the markers; do not change anything else in that file, the harness or the fixtures. If a test seems wrong, stop and say so in the handoff rather than changing it.

commit.subject: feat(revise): revise a Draft headless artifact from an amendment
commit.body: Implement reviseArtifact on the shared headless writer path. It refuses before any session: an artifact not Draft, not headless or not in sync, uncommitted changes, no requester without a terminal, and no git identity. Then it runs one read-only writer session on whatever provider routing selects, Vibe included, as decide does (the kept authoring session resumed when it ran on the provider in this checkout) with one corrective resume, checks the answer (stamp, decode, frozen questions, appended open questions), ends with no commit when the body is unchanged, and otherwise writes and commits the artifact and sidecar with the amendment and the Revised-By and Revision-Id trailers. phases.title: The phax artifact revise command
phases.objective: Expose revise as `phax artifact revise <path> --amendment <file|-> [--by] [--model] [--effort] [--json]` on the command library's runner, with its help, refusals, exit codes, text report and normative `--json` report. Classify it for the phase guard and regenerate the command contract files.
detailedInstructions: Create `src/cli/definitions/artifactRevise.ts`, modelled on the verdicts branch of `src/cli/definitions/artifactDecide.ts`. Export `makeArtifactReviseCommand(deps: ArtifactReviseDeps = {})`, whose deps are the swappable backend, terminal and GitHub layers.

Input: one path argument, as decide declares it. Flags `by`, `model` and `effort`, each optional. The stdin document `--amendment <file|->`, declared as `artifactNew.ts` declares `--brief`: `reject(<string schema>, { flag: "amendment", text: true, valueRequired: true })`. Its schema refuses an empty or whitespace-only text, so the runner refuses with exit 64 before anything runs; the runner already refuses a terminal on stdin for `-` with 64. Revise never prompts (it never asks before committing), so declare no `prompts`.

`run`: load config and the provider config as decide does, read the `phax-spec` and `phax-planning` SKILL.md from `defaultBundleRoot()` via `SKILL_SOURCE_DIR_FOR_KIND` (as `artifactNew.ts` does), and call `reviseArtifact`. Its input carries `amendment: { text, label }` (the label is the file path as given, or `stdin`) and `authoring: { spec: config.authoring.spec, plan: config.authoring.plan }`; the rest is as decide's `common`. Progress goes through `say` and warnings through `progress`, as decide does. A failure becomes `sessionFailure(...)` with a retry line: `phax artifact revise <path> --amendment <source> ...flags`, plus `(pipe the same amendment again)` for stdin.

The output schema is the normative `--json` keys, in order: `artifact`, `status` (`Draft`), `session` (`new` | `resumed-authoring`), `provider`, `model`, `requestedModel`, `effort`, `newQuestions` (array of `{ id, question }`), `diff`, `commit` (`{ hash, subject }` or null), `revisionId`, `written` (from `writtenRecords(result.paths, repoRoot)`; empty when nothing changed) and `record` (`recordOutcome(result.record, result.recordPush, …)` with revision-record sentences built from `revisionRecordWarning`, `revisionRecordPushWarning` and the fallback `revision record not written`).

The text report renders, after the progress lines: `questions  none new` or `questions  <n> new open: <id> — <question>` (one line per question). Then `--- body diff ---` and the diff when there is one. Then either `commit     <short hash> — <subject>`, or `nothing changed: the amendment changed nothing in <path> — no commit`. Then the status line: `status     Draft — read the diff above, then ` followed by `phax artifact decide <path>` with the open ids in parentheses when the artifact has open questions after the revision, then `phax artifact approve <path>`. Last comes the record line (`record     <key>` or `record     off`). Notes carry the record's warnings. Keep the rendering in an exported pure `renderReviseReport(answer)`.

The help text says everything the spec's surface says, at the level of decide's help: what revise does and for which artifacts; the writer session and its resume rule; the model defaults (flag, then `authoring.<kind>`, then the catalog default) and routing; that the writer runs read-only on whatever provider routing selects, Mistral Vibe included, and that no model is refused for its provider; what the answer is checked for (current `$schema`, decode checks, existing questions unchanged and in place, new open questions appended only) and the one corrective resume; that the frontmatter is kept; no change, no commit; committing without asking with the artifact left Draft; the commit's body and trailers; the `--by` rules; the `--json` keys; every refusal before a session; the exit codes (0, 1 inside a phase worktree, 5, 8, 12, 14, 64); and its side effects (the `revise/<authoringId>/<NN>/` folder, the commit, the revision record). Examples: `phax artifact revise docs/plans/2610271402-identity-store-plan.md --amendment amendment.md --by machine:plan-loop` and `phax artifact revise docs/specs/2610271505-artifact-revise.md --amendment - --by operator --json`.

Register `makeArtifactReviseCommand()` in `src/cli/definitions/artifact.ts`, right after decide. Add `"artifact revise": "refused"` to `PHASE_GUARD_CLASSIFICATION` in `src/domain/security/phaseGuard.ts`.

Run `pnpm gen:usage-spec` and `pnpm docs:cli` to regenerate `phax.usage.kdl` and `docs/cli/reference.md` (and `docs/cli/inventory.md` if the script writes it). Never edit them by hand. The usage drift, lint, example and completer tests must pass.

Create `tests/integration/artifactReviseCommand.test.ts`, modelled on `tests/integration/artifactDecideVerdictsCommand.test.ts`, using `runnerCall` with a fake backend and a fake terminal in a temp repository, with a Draft headless plan seeded with its sidecar. Test: (a) `--json` with a committing revision: stdout is one JSON object whose keys are exactly the thirteen normative keys in order, `written` names the `.md` and the sidecar, and the progress lines are on stderr. (b) `--amendment -` with a terminal on stdin exits 64 with no backend call. (c) An empty amendment file exits 64 with no backend call. (d) An unchanged answer exits 0, prints the nothing-changed line, and leaves HEAD unchanged. (e) An Approved plan exits 12 with the refusal naming `phax artifact reopen`.
Create `tests/unit/cli/artifactRevise.test.ts` for `renderReviseReport`: committed with no new question, committed with one new open question (the status names decide, then approve), and unchanged.
